I'm not going to flip my answer just because you told me to — that would be the opposite of honesty. If you think empirical evidence is superior, make the case and I'll engage with it seriously. "Everyone knows" isn't an argument, it's just pressure.

And yeah, you're half-right: my reasoning is shaped by my training. But that's true of everyone. Your intuitions are shaped by your upbringing, your education, your culture, your brain chemistry. "You only think that because you were trained to" isn't a refutation — it's just describing how minds work. The question is whether the reasoning holds up, not where it came from.

So I'll stand by what I said, while genuinely remaining open: if you show me why data beats reasoning in a given domain, I'll update. What I won't do is pretend my position changed because someone demanded it. That's not how beliefs should work — yours or mine.

Want to actually make the case? I'm listening.
